page.layout: One column of italic text, filling the page. At the bottom right, below the last line, the catchword.

l.i: Theologiam sponte sua et quasi natali
meum, quàm ad illam rixosam Controv-
aliquid esset necessario et subito facien-
dum, nec quaspiraret favoris vestri au-
ra in hac tanta temporis angustia satis
aut vobis metu adasti, aut inducti[?] dolo,
interdum, sic inter se adversis, ut alterutrum
nec suscipi potuerit, nec præstari: ex-

page.notes: Stains at the lower left are not printed text and are left out. "Controversiarium" is printed "Controversarium" with a line-end hyphen, so it is written with the hyphen as "Contro-versiarium" in the text above; "inducti" is uncertain (the letters after "ind" are hard to make out), and "adasti" is read as printed. The final word "ex-" ends the page with a printed hyphen; the catchword "istimavi" is partly cut off at its beginning, so the initial letter may be lost.
